# Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, established in 2019, describes itself as advancing AI research, education, and policy to improve the human condition. The institute operates from Stanford's campus in California as a university-based research lab, viewing AI as a field that spans the entire university and requiring interdisciplinary expertise across many departments. Its core vision emphasizes studying, guiding, and developing human-centered AI technologies that are collaborative, augmentative, and enhance human productivity and quality of life rather than replace workers.

The institute's work spans research, education, and policy development. Clinical Mind AI is a Stanford-developed platform designed to strengthen clinical reasoning education through AI-simulated patient encounters across health professions, created by Marcos Santiago Rojas Pino and Thomas Caruso. The institute offers specialized training programs for policymakers and civil servants on AI governance, courses for business leaders and decision-makers, and programs focused on the K-12 ecosystem including teachers and students. Its research includes studies on AI companions and well-being, and work at Stanford Law School building an AI pipeline to analyze local statutes across the country. The institute also produces the AI Index, described as providing the most comprehensive analysis of AI's trajectory available, and hosts the Joint California Summit on Generative AI highlighted in Governor Newsom's Executive Order.

The institute operates through fellowship programs supporting researchers at disciplinary intersections and maintains Affinity Groups for students. Its policy work, conducted through evidence-based research and global convenings, focuses on equipping decision-makers with insights into AI governance. Co-Directors Fei-Fei Li and John Etchemendy lead the organization, which operates as a nonprofit institution.
